items.details: Pick up rental car at Cancun Airport, drive 2 hours to Chiquila. Park car (100 pesos / $5 per 24h). Ferry to Isla Holbox every half hour, ~200 pesos ($10) adult.
items.name: Cancun to Holbox transfer

items.details: Recommended luxury stay on Holbox; she stayed here on her first trip. Beachfront area, pool, romantic room design, outstanding food.
items.name: Ser Casasandra

items.details: Mid-range adults-only hotel a few blocks from town; great pool, bohemian decor; she stayed here on second trip.
items.name: Hotel Para Ti

items.details: Budget hostel in the center of town; rooms small and basic but clean.
items.name: Hotelito Villas Holbox

items.details: Hostel option on Holbox; can get loud at night.
items.name: Tribu

items.details: Boat trip from Holbox to this inlet with the clearest, most beautiful water; she calls it a must. A Viator tour (snorkeling and/or fishing) is linked.
items.name: Cabo Catoche boat trip

items.details: Popular boat trip to Bird Island, uninhabited Pasion Island (sandbar walk), and Cenote Yalahau on the mainland.
items.name: Three-island boat trip

items.details: Available June through September; peak season July and August. Called one of the coolest activities in Mexico.
items.name: Swim with whale sharks

items.details: Popular sunset spot on Holbox for cocktails at sunset.
items.name: Zomay

items.details: Recommended breakfast stop on the mainland in Chiquila before driving on.
items.name: La Sardina Enamorada

items.details: Ferry back to Chiquila, pick up car, drive just over 2 hours to Valladolid, crossing from Quintana Roo into Yucatan state (1 hour time change).
items.name: Drive to Valladolid

items.details: Luxury pick in Valladolid; described as possibly the most beautiful property in town with chic colorful rooms, outdoor hammocks and pool.
items.name: Le Muuch Hotel

items.details: Mid-range property in Valladolid that feels luxurious: classy stone bathtubs, elegant carved wood furniture, well priced and central.
items.name: Casa Tia Micha

items.details: Budget hotel in Valladolid; simple but clean, recently renovated, a few blocks from Cenote Zaci.
items.name: Hotel Zazil-Maj

items.details: Head to the ruins first thing in the morning; opens 8:00 AM, 45 minutes from Valladolid. Go early to beat crowds; avoid Sundays (free admission for Mexicans = very crowded). UNESCO World Heritage Site, Temple of Kukulkan.
items.name: Chichen Itza

items.details: Cenote right in downtown Valladolid with waterfalls; one of the deepest cenotes in the region; recently reopened after renovations.
items.name: Cenote Zaci

items.details: Her favorite cenote in the region: visually spectacular, large, not too touristed, lovely grounds, surprisingly good food. Alternative: Cenote Ik-Kil (similar look, more crowded).
items.name: Hacienda San Lorenzo Oxman cenote

items.details: Gelato cafe in Valladolid; hard-to-find good gelato in Mexico, limited but inventive flavors (she loved the rosemary).
items.name: Wabi Gelato

items.details: Cafe on Calzada de los Frailes; she had a great pay de limon (lemon pie) here.
items.name: ConKafecito

items.details: Remaining route per her day-by-day plan: Day 6 Valladolid to Rio Lagartos; Day 7 to Merida via Izamal; Days 8-10 Merida and day trips (Uxmal, Celestun, Izamal, Campeche); Day 11 Merida to Bacalar (Lake of Seven Colors); Days 12-13 Bacalar; Day 14 Bacalar back to Cancun Airport. Notable: this itinerary deliberately skips Cancun, Playa del Carmen and Tulum.
items.name: Days 6-14 route outline (Rio Lagartos, Merida, Bacalar)

itineraries.summary: Kate McCulley's two-week Yucatan road trip itinerary skips Cancun, Playa del Carmen and Tulum in favor of Isla Holbox, colonial Valladolid, Rio Lagartos, Merida with cenote and ruin day trips, and the Lake of Seven Colors at Bacalar. It is a full day-by-day plan with named hotel, restaurant and activity recommendations at each stop, based on her winter living in Merida and years of trips through the peninsula.
itineraries.title: Two Weeks in Mexico: The BEST Yucatan Road Trip Itinerary

items.details: Explore the UNESCO World Heritage Old City early before the heat; hire a local guide (Dubrovnik Tourist Board office outside Pile Gate) or get lost on your own through hidden pathways and staircases.
items.name: Explore Dubrovnik Old Town

items.details: Pass covering City Walls access, small museums/galleries (she liked the Franciscan Monastery), free public transport and discounts. Summer 2025 pricing: 40 EUR ($44) 1-day, 50 EUR ($55) 3-day, 60 EUR ($66) 7-day.
items.name: Dubrovnik Pass

items.details: Her favorite restaurant in Dubrovnik since 2014; Michelin-recommended seafood. Known for tartares, pasta with shrimp and Istrian truffles, and fish cooked in a crust of salt.
items.name: Proto

items.details: Capon (castrated rooster) specialist in the Old City, open Mar 15 - Nov 15; alternative for non-seafood eaters. Capon truffle gnocchi was one of the best things she ate in Dubrovnik.
items.name: Kopun

items.details: Cable car to the top of Mount Srd; go about an hour before sunset for the best colors. Round trip 27 EUR ($28) adults, 7 EUR ($7) children 4-12.
items.name: Dubrovnik Cable Car

items.details: Dinner atop Mount Srd with panoramic views; surprisingly great food. Tip: call and book a table with the best view at least a month ahead. Open mid March to mid November.
items.name: Panorama Restaurant

items.details: Wine bar in the Old City run by an Australian man and Croatian wife; great place to try Croatian wines by the glass (Dingac reds from Peljesac; Grk and Posip whites from Korcula).
items.name: D'Vino Wine Bar

items.details: Morning sea kayak around the Old City with views of the Old Town; tours from $43 USD including a snorkeling break on a secluded beach; solo kayak rentals also available. Lokrum Island is a possible longer option.
items.name: Sea kayaking around the Old City

items.details: Her three beach picks: City Beach (adjacent to Old City), Pasjaca Beach (35-min drive south, most beautiful but rugged path), Sveti Jakov Beach (8-min drive south, locals' favorite). No private beaches in Croatia - all are public.
items.name: Beach morning options

items.details: Walk the walls ~2 hours before closing to avoid midday heat. High season 40 EUR ($42) adults; low season 15 EUR ($16). About two hours, one-way counterclockwise.
items.name: Walk the City Walls at sunset

items.details: Her lunch recommendations in the Old Town: Kamenice (mussels fresh from the sea), Bota Sare Oyster and Sushi Bar (oysters and sushi), Pizzeria Castro (pizza, heard good things), Dolce Vita (gelato, bitter orange + dark chocolate).
items.name: Lunch spots: Kamenice, Bota Sare, Pizzeria Castro, Dolce Vita

items.details: Traditional Croatian peka dinner (octopus or lamb/veal cooked under the bell with potatoes over coals) hosted by locals Marija and Zlatko in their backyard, with cured meats, cheeses, liqueurs and local wine. Book via Dubrovnik Eat With Locals; ~$100 USD per person.
items.name: Peka dinner with Marija & Zlatko

items.details: Morning visit to the island next to Dubrovnik (City of Qarth in Game of Thrones); rock slab beaches, botanical gardens, Benedictine monastery, Iron Throne at the free visitor center. Ferry 7 EUR ($7) each way, 15 min, up to 25x daily in peak season. Half day recommended.
items.name: Visit Lokrum Island

items.details: Day trip to her favorite quiet Croatian island: dense forest, neon-blue saltwater lakes; rent a bike in Mljet National Park, hike 45 min to Montokuc viewpoint, swim in saltwater lakes, visit the monastery on St. Mary's Island. Early morning ferry to Polace (90 min, 10 EUR each way). Lunch: pizza and beer at Pizzeria Levanat in Pomena.
items.name: Mljet Island day trip
items.price_hint: Ferry 10 EUR ($10) each way to Polace

items.details: Interactive museum of Croatia's communist/Yugoslavia era near the Gruz ferry port; 90 minutes is enough. Entry 9 EUR ($9) adults.
items.name: Red History Museum

items.details: Dubrovnik was King's Landing; a mainland tour covers most filming sites in 2-3 hours. A Viator tour is linked; check whether Lokrum Island is included (most mainland tours skip it).
items.name: Game of Thrones tour

itineraries.summary: Kate's three-day Dubrovnik itinerary paces Old Town exploration, beach/pool downtime and sunset experiences instead of racing through sights. Day 1 covers the Old City, lunch at her favorite restaurant Proto, the cable car to Mount Srd and dinner at Panorama; Day 2 is sea kayaking, beaches, the City Walls at sunset and a traditional peka feast with locals; Day 3 offers Lokrum Island, Mljet Island, the Red History Museum or a Game of Thrones tour.
itineraries.title: The Best 3 Day Dubrovnik Itinerary

extractions.notes: @adventurouskate is travel blogger Kate McCulley; her Instagram promotes her blog's deep itinerary guides. Both itineraries are full day-by-day plans from her own site with named hotels, restaurants, activities and prices; confidence high. She also publishes many more itineraries (Northern Italy 21-day, Croatia 2-week, Nova Scotia, Cabot Trail, Mexico).

items.details: Arrival at Kilimanjaro International Airport (JRO); private transfer to lodge in Arusha with dinner. Meal plan: dinner.
items.name: Airport arrival and transfer

items.details: Overnight lodge in Arusha on arrival night (budget category).
items.name: Airport Planet Lodge

items.details: Drive to Serengeti National Park via Masai countryside; first game drive on entry. Central Serengeti (Seronera) noted for one of Africa's highest densities of big cats (lions, leopards, cheetahs). Full board.
items.name: Arusha to Central Serengeti game drive

items.details: Overnight lodge in Central Serengeti (budget category).
items.name: Serengeti Simba Lodge

items.details: Game viewing en route toward the Northern Serengeti, the heart of the Great Migration river-crossing zone around the Mara River. Full board.
items.name: Drive to Northern Serengeti

items.details: Overnight lodge in Northern Serengeti (budget category).
items.name: Baobab Mara North

items.details: Entire day exploring the Mara River region; with luck, witness wildebeest/zebra river crossings into crocodile-filled waters. Lions, cheetahs, leopards, hyenas and crocodiles very active. Full board.
items.name: Great Migration river crossings

items.details: Early morning game drive exiting the north, watching for predators after an active night; game drives en route back to Central Serengeti (resident lion prides, high leopard densities, Seronera River ecosystem).
items.name: Morning game drive south

items.details: Overnight lodge in Central Serengeti (budget category).
items.name: Baobab Central

items.details: Drive into Ngorongoro Conservation Area; descend 600m into the crater, the world's largest natural wildlife arena: black rhino, lions, buffalo, hippos, hyenas, seasonal flamingos. Unhurried crater tour with packed lunch. Full board.
items.name: Ngorongoro Crater game drive

items.details: Overnight lodge in Karatu (budget category).
items.name: Farm of Dreams Lodge

items.details: Relaxed breakfast, then drive back through highlands and Maasai plains to Arusha/Kilimanjaro for onward flight. Breakfast only.
items.name: Departure transfer

items.details: Also included in the package: private 4x4 Land Cruiser with pop-up roof, professional English-speaking safari guide, unlimited game drives, all park entrance and concession fees, Ngorongoro crater descent fees, all airport transfers, AMREF Flying Doctors evacuation cover, complimentary Maasai village visit.
items.name: Safari package inclusions
items.price_hint: From USD 3,326.32 per person (budget, 2 guests, high season, land only)

itineraries.summary: A 7-day Great Migration safari from Kilimanjaro/Arusha through Central and Northern Serengeti to the Mara River river-crossing zone and back via the Ngorongoro Crater. Full day-by-day plan with named lodges each night, meal plans, and a priced package (from USD 3,326.32 pp budget, 2 guests, high season) including private 4x4, guide, unlimited game drives and all park fees.
itineraries.title: 7-Day Wild & Free Tanzania Great Migration Safari

items.details: Scenic drive from Nairobi through the Great Rift Valley; afternoon game drive at Lake Nakuru National Park, famous for flamingo-lined shores, white and black rhinos, birdlife, buffalo, Rothschild's giraffe, leopards and tree-climbing lions.
items.name: Nairobi to Lake Nakuru game drive

items.details: Drive via farmlands and Maasai homesteads to the Masai Mara National Reserve; lunch, then afternoon game drive - Big Five and plains game.
items.name: Nakuru to Masai Mara

items.details: Early-morning and full-day exploration of the Mara; during Jul-Oct, the Great Wildebeest Migration and Mara River crossings. Visit to a traditional Maasai village for a cultural encounter.
items.name: Full-day Mara safari + Maasai village

items.details: Sunrise game drive, then check out and drive back to Nairobi. End of tour.
items.name: Return to Nairobi

itineraries.summary: A short, high-impact 4-day Kenya safari combining flamingo-fringed Rift Valley lakes (Lake Nakuru) with the Masai Mara's Big Five and a Maasai village cultural visit. Day-by-day structure is clear, but the source names only generic overnight locations (Nakuru, Masai Mara), so confidence is medium.
itineraries.title: 4 Days Kenya's Golden Safari Circuit - Rift Valley Lakes & the Wild Mara

extractions.notes: @africansafari could not be verified as a distinct personal Instagram influencer account; the handle matches africansafari.co.in, an Indian safari tour operator (associated with Norine Forbes Safaris/Tourips Tours). The itineraries extracted are the company's own published, priced, day-by-day safari products, which is exactly what the account promotes. Treat identity linkage as assumed, not verified.

items.details: Drive from Pokhara back to Kathmandu, 7-8 hours. Farewell dinner included in package.
items.name: Return to Kathmandu

items.details: Package includes: airport pickup/drop-off, 3-star hotel in Kathmandu on B/B plan, land transport, TIMS permit, equipped/insured trekking porter (1 per 2 persons, carries 25kg), experienced first-aid-trained English-speaking guide, full-board camping with three meals daily, camping crew. Grade: easy. Best season: spring/autumn.
items.name: Package inclusions

itineraries.summary: A 7-day easy-grade guided trek in the Pokhara region: arrival in Kathmandu, travel to Pokhara, then a 4-day village-to-village trek through Kalikasthan, Syaklung and Chisapani Danda with a return via Begnas Tal. Full day-by-day route with elevations, included guide/porter/permits/meals listed; specific trek lodges not named, so confidence is medium.
